instructions: Cut the onion into quarters and halve the ginger lengthwise. Heat a large dry pot over medium-high heat and set the onion and ginger in it, cut sides down. Leave them for 4 minutes, until the cut sides are charred.
Add the star anise, cloves, cinnamon stick and coriander seeds and stir for 1 minute, until they smell toasty.
Pour in the broth and 1 cup water, add 2 tbsp of the tamari and bring it to a boil. Turn the heat to low, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice noodles following the package directions. Drain them and rinse under cold water.
Cut the tofu into 3/4-inch cubes and pat them dry. Toss them with the cornstarch and 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the tofu in a single layer and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until most sides are golden. Transfer it to a plate.
Stem the shiitakes and slice the caps. Halve the bok choy lengthwise. Chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro and cut the lime into wedges.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in the same skillet over high heat. Add the shiitakes and a pinch of the remaining salt and cook for 4 minutes, stirring only now and then, until they're browned.
Set the bok choy cut side down in the skillet and cook for 1 minute. Add the rice vinegar and 2 tbsp water, cover, turn the heat to medium and cook for 5 minutes, until the bok choy is tender.
Strain the broth through a fine strainer into a clean pot and discard the solids. Bring it back to a simmer.
Divide the noodles between 4 bowls. Add the tofu, shiitakes and bok choy, then ladle the hot broth over them. Top with the bean sprouts and cilantro.
Taste the broth. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve with the lime wedges and the sriracha, and the rest of the tamari for the table.
method_notes: Love and Lemons' vegan pho (4.73 from 51 ratings) is the lead: char the onion and ginger, toast the spices, simmer the broth, then top rice noodles with browned shiitakes, bok choy and tofu. Its hour is cut to about 45 minutes by charring the onion and ginger in the pot instead of under the broiler, using vegetable broth in place of water and kombu, and a 20 minute simmer. The tofu is pan-seared in cornstarch rather than baked, as in My Plantiful Cooking's Tofu Pho. The Food Blog's 30 minute version (5 from 18 ratings) confirms the short simmer. Tamari and rice noodles keep it gluten-free, and heat is left to the sriracha at the table.
